m-extensor-carpi-radialis-longus.summary: A muscle on the posterolateral (radial) forearm running just behind brachioradialis; it steadies the wrist when making a fist.
facts: Lower 1/3 of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus and lateral intermuscular septum
Dorsal surface of the base of the 2nd metacarpal
Radial nerve (C6–C7)
Radial recurrent artery, radial artery
Extends and abducts the wrist (radial deviation)
tus: It receives a branch directly from the main trunk of the radial nerve before the deep branch arises; it is therefore spared in lesions in the supinator canal (posterior interosseous nerve), and the wrist deviates radially.

m-extensor-carpi-radialis-brevis.summary: A muscle beneath the long radial extensor arising from the common extensor tendon; the commonest source of lateral epicondylitis.
facts: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon) and radial collateral ligament
Dorsal surface of the base of the 3rd metacarpal
Deep branch of the radial nerve (C7–C8)
Radial recurrent artery, radial artery
Extends and abducts the wrist
clinical: Lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) is most often a tendinopathy of this muscle's origin; resisted wrist extension and middle finger extension are painful.

m-extensor-digiti-minimi.summary: A slender muscle separated from the medial side of extensor digitorum; its tendon runs through the 5th extensor compartment.
facts: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon)
Dorsal aponeurosis of the 5th finger
Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of the radial nerve, C7–C8)
Posterior interosseous artery
Extends the little finger

m-extensor-indicis.summary: A muscle in the deep posterior layer of the forearm that allows independent extension of the index finger.
facts: Lower part of the posterior surface of the ulna and interosseous membrane
Dorsal aponeurosis of the index finger (ulnar side of the extensor digitorum tendon)
Posterior interosseous nerve (C7–C8)
Posterior interosseous artery
Extends the index finger independently
tus: It is a commonly used donor tendon in tendon transfers (e.g. for EPL rupture).

m-abductor-pollicis-longus.summary: A muscle arising from the deep posterior layer of the forearm and running to the thumb; its tendon runs with EPB in the 1st extensor compartment.
facts: Posterior surfaces of the ulna and radius and interosseous membrane
Lateral surface of the base of the 1st metacarpal
Posterior interosseous nerve (C7–C8)
Posterior interosseous artery
Abducts and extends the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint; assists wrist abduction
clinical: In De Quervain's tenosynovitis the APL and EPB tendons in the 1st extensor compartment are inflamed; Finkelstein's test is positive.
tus: With EPB it forms the lateral (radial) border of the anatomical snuffbox.

m-extensor-pollicis-brevis.summary: A short muscle just beneath APL that accompanies it.
facts: Posterior surface of the radius and interosseous membrane
Dorsal surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
Posterior interosseous nerve (C7–C8)
Posterior interosseous artery
Extends the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint

m-extensor-pollicis-longus.summary: A muscle whose tendon turns around the dorsal tubercle of the radius (Lister's) to reach the distal phalanx of the thumb.
facts: Middle 1/3 of the posterior surface of the ulna and interosseous membrane
Dorsal surface of the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
Posterior interosseous nerve (C7–C8)
Posterior interosseous artery
Extends the thumb at the interphalangeal and MCP joints
clinical: After a distal radius fracture (especially by friction at Lister's tubercle) the tendon may rupture ('drummer's palsy'); the tip of the thumb cannot be lifted.
tus: It is the medial (ulnar) border of the anatomical snuffbox; the floor of the snuffbox contains the scaphoid and the radial artery.

m-abductor-pollicis-brevis.summary: The most superficial and most lateral muscle of the thenar eminence.
facts: Flexor retinaculum, tubercle of the scaphoid and tubercle of the trapezium
Radial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
Recurrent branch of the median nerve (C8–T1)
Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery
Abducts the thumb at right angles to the plane of the palm
clinical: It is among the first muscles to waste in carpal tunnel syndrome; strength of palmar abduction is reduced.

m-flexor-pollicis-brevis.summary: A thenar muscle with superficial and deep heads, each supplied by a different nerve.
facts: Superficial head: flexor retinaculum and trapezium; deep head: trapezoid and capitate
Radial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb (radial sesamoid)
Superficial head: median nerve (recurrent branch); deep head: deep branch of the ulnar nerve
Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery
Flexes the thumb at the MCP joint
tus: It is the thenar muscle with a dual nerve supply, so it may be partly spared in median nerve lesions.

m-opponens-pollicis.summary: A thenar muscle deep to the short abductor, attached along the whole length of the 1st metacarpal.
facts: Flexor retinaculum and tubercle of the trapezium
Whole radial border of the 1st metacarpal
Recurrent branch of the median nerve (C8–T1)
Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery
Opposes the thumb to the other fingers (opposition: flexion, abduction and medial rotation)
clinical: Superficial cuts of the recurrent branch of the median nerve (the 'million-dollar nerve') abolish opposition, producing an ape-hand appearance.

m-adductor-pollicis.summary: A triangular muscle deep in the palm with oblique and transverse heads; the thenar-region muscle supplied by the ulnar nerve.
facts: Oblique head: capitate and bases of the 2nd–3rd metacarpals; transverse head: palmar surface of the 3rd metacarpal
Ulnar side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb (ulnar sesamoid)
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8–T1)
Deep palmar arch
Adducts the thumb; contributes to grip strength
clinical: In ulnar nerve palsy, when the patient tries to hold paper between thumb and index finger, the thumb flexes using FPL (Froment's sign).

m-abductor-digiti-minimi-manus.summary: The most superficial and most medial muscle of the hypothenar eminence.
facts: Pisiform and tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris
Ulnar side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8–T1)
Deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery
Abducts the little finger

m-flexor-digiti-minimi-manus.summary: A hypothenar muscle lying lateral to the abductor.
facts: Hook of the hamate and flexor retinaculum
Base of the proximal phalanx of the 5th finger
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
Deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery
Flexes the little finger at the MCP joint

m-opponens-digiti-minimi-manus.summary: The deepest hypothenar muscle; it attaches to the ulnar border of the 5th metacarpal.
facts: Hook of the hamate and flexor retinaculum
Ulnar border of the 5th metacarpal
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
Deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery
Draws the 5th metacarpal forwards and laterally to oppose it to the thumb (cups the palm)
tus: The deep branch of the ulnar nerve winds around the hook of the hamate, passing between the abductor and the short flexor and piercing this muscle.

mm-interossei-dorsales-manus.summary: Four two-headed muscles between the metacarpals; they spread the fingers away from the axis of the middle finger.
facts: Facing surfaces of two adjacent metacarpals (two heads)
Bases of the proximal phalanges and dorsal aponeurosis: radial side of the 2nd finger, both sides of the 3rd, ulnar side of the 4th
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8–T1)
Deep palmar arch, dorsal metacarpal arteries
Abduct the fingers (DAB); flex the MCP and extend the interphalangeal joints
tus: Dorsal ABduct (DAB), palmar ADduct (PAD); the 1st dorsal interosseous is the first to show wasting in ulnar nerve palsy (hollowing of the first web space).

mm-interossei-palmares.summary: Three (four in some sources) single-headed muscles on the palmar surface of the metacarpals; they bring the fingers towards the middle finger.
facts: Palmar surfaces of the 2nd, 4th and 5th metacarpals facing the middle finger (single heads)
Base of the proximal phalanx and dorsal aponeurosis of the same finger
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve (C8–T1)
Deep palmar arch, palmar metacarpal arteries
Adduct the fingers (PAD); MCP flexion and IP extension
clinical: In ulnar nerve palsy the card test (holding paper between the fingers) is weak; loss of the interossei contributes to the claw hand.
